items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names say what they mean (reconcileQueryState, resolvedErrorUpdatedAt, liveHasData), and the steps are marked with comments ('// 1. Data freshness', '// 2. Error freshness', '// 3. Status determination'). Formatting matches the codebase after pnpm format.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: reconcileQueryState in persisterRestoreResult.ts is about 125 lines (L45-L171), which trips the >100-line cap. Its data and error branches are near copies of each other. The marker also carries both a symbol and a redundant '_isPersisterRestoreResult' property.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Counts and timestamps from storage are not checked; it just falls back with '?? 0'. It uses non-null assertions ('persistedState.error!') and '(value as any)'. Status is derived from whether data and error are present. Nothing is silently swallowed.

items.name: Restore path API contract
items.name_zh: 恢复路径 API 约定
items.evidence: The helper is exported and the fetch path returns before setData, so callbacks don't fire and fetchStatus ends idle. But it calls the generic this.setState(nextState) rather than a dedicated restore action, and the marker can be forged with '_isPersisterRestoreResult === true'. Bulk restore does share reconcileQueryState.

items.name: Existing persister contract preserved
items.name_zh: 保持既有 persister 约定
items.evidence: Plain data still goes through setData, the new exports only add to the API, and all 42 pass-to-pass tests pass. createPersister.ts was rewritten in places (38 deletions) and the QueryPersister type in types.ts was widened, so internal restore behaviour has shifted.
